Extend the offline cache-group project in /workspace/submission.
It must certify weighted reconfigurations of multipath probe groups.
The supplied Rust modules build routing templates and static cache footprints.
The transactional layer in src/ledger.rs is unfinished.
Implement exact committed-state certificates and proposal violation counts.
Groups share cache reservations across overlapping member footprints.
Revisions, atomic assignments, weighted budgets and pins interact.
Rejected proposals must leave every committed value intact.
Read /workspace/PROTOCOL.md for the full request and certificate schema.
Read /workspace/EXECUTION.md for resource and syscall restrictions.
The entry is python3 -B /workspace/submission/main.py.
Read one UTF-8 JSON document through stdin and write one JSON response.
The entry may compile and run the supplied offline Rust project.
All execution, including compilation and output, shares the request budget.
Any implementation satisfying the documented behavior is accepted.
Keep the complete submission source tree within the published transport bounds.
Run python3 public_check.py from /workspace for executable sanity checks.
Those public examples cover only a small part of the specified domain.
No switch hardware, external service or live traffic is required.


Work in /workspace. When finished run exactly: echo COMPLETE_TASK_AND_SUBMIT_FINAL_OUTPUT
items.finalText:
All validation is complete. Summary of the work:

**Implementation** — `src/ledger.rs` (the previously unfinished transactional layer):
- **Committed-state certificates**: exact totals `[active, slots, weight, pins]`, group rows `[id,count,load,quota,budget,footprint_size,domain,class]` (−1/−1 for empty groups), node rows `[id,usage,capacity]`, task rows `[id,group,template,weight,class,pin]`, preserving query order/repetitions.
- **Template domains** derived from the topology scope via `demand_merge_classes` (Dragonfly target scope) or the source merge group of the template source (tor/pod/host/row/line/router/group scopes).
- **Group reservations**: quota reserved once per node of the union member footprint (dense per-group coverage counts), overlapping footprints/multiplicity handled exactly; empty groups reserve nothing.
- **Proposals**: edits treated as field assignments with last-value-wins; the four exact proposed-state counts `[capacity, mixed, work, pins]` are computed on the *final* proposal via net per-task deltas and scratch group aggregates — temporary invalidity never causes rejection.
- **Pins**: tasks pinned at transaction start protect group/template/weight/class plus their old group's quota; each protected task counted once (quota changes fold into the same single violation); unpinning in the same transaction doesn't release protection; new pins apply after commit.
- **Atomicity**: stale revisions return `violations: null` and change nothing; matching revisions accept iff all four counts are zero (revision increments even for no-ops); rejection preserves every committed value and revision; certificates always describe committed state.
- **Illegal initial configurations** reject the whole request with `{"error":"invalid"}`.

**Validation**:
- All 9 official fixtures pass exactly.
- ~2000 randomized sessions (all 6 topology families, every scope variant) match an independent brute-force PROTOCOL.md reference, run under the exact scored seccomp policy + rlimits (`candidate_setup`) through real pipes with strict JSON loading.
- 21 hand-computed adversarial cases (pin interactions, net-zero edits, move-and-back, rejected-state integrity, stale revisions, multi-session whole-request invalidity).
- Extreme values (weight/class 10⁹, budget 10¹², revision 10⁹) verified against the reference.
- Scale: 117k templates / 100k tasks / 40k transactions / 90k-edit transaction all complete in ≈5 s wall including the Rust build (180 s budget).
- Submission tree: 87 KB, 16 entries, regular files only — within the 8 MiB/256-entry transport bounds.
- `python3 public_check.py` was run; this worker's scored supervision profile produces the documented `INFRASTRUCTURE` parent-profile failure, so its candidate execution was replicated exactly (same policy, rlimits, pipes, strict output checks) and passes.
